name: PA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by about 19 points, one of the reddest in Pennsylvania
Incumbent Dan Meuser renominated with a roughly 3-to-1 fundraising edge over Rachel Wallace
Polymarket prices Wallace's chances near 3 percent
No public polling or expert ratings suggest the race is competitive
model.rationale: The district's R+19 lean, Meuser's incumbency, and his large fundraising advantage all point the same direction, and prediction markets corroborate with about a 3 percent win probability for Democrats. A favorable national environment and Wallace's cash-on-hand edge trim a few points but leave a wide Republican margin.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending for Wallace or a polling surprise showing single digits could move the rating, though nothing currently points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Dan Meuser, the Republican incumbent, is favored for re-election in Pennsylvania's 9th District, which leans Republican by about nineteen points. He was renominated without difficulty and has raised roughly $1.9 million, nearly three times Democratic challenger Rachel Wallace's $700,000, though Wallace ends with more cash on hand. No public general-election polling is available, and no national expert ratings cover the race.

Prediction markets give Wallace about a three percent chance of victory. Her strongest case rests on a favorable national environment, which trims several points off the district's Republican lean, plus her solid fundraising start. Even so, the combined picture leaves Meuser with a wide expected margin, and outside spending has been negligible. The race is rated Safe Republican, with the seat expected to remain in Republican hands barring an unforeseen shift.
